nodes.title: ISTQB CTFL v4.0.1
nodes.summary: The Foundation Level syllabus in six chapters. The exam has 40 multiple-choice questions, 60 minutes and a pass mark of 65% (26 correct).
points: Questions per chapter follow the syllabus weighting
K1 = remember, K2 = understand, K3 = apply
Chapter 4 carries the most questions (11)

nodes.title: 1 · Fundamentals of Testing
nodes.summary: What testing is, why it is needed, the seven principles and the test process.
points: 8 exam questions
180 minutes of study time in the syllabus

nodes.title: 1.1 What is Testing?
nodes.summary: Testing is a set of activities to discover defects and evaluate the quality of software work products. It covers verification and validation, static and dynamic testing.
points: Objectives: evaluate work products, trigger failures and find defects, ensure coverage, reduce risk, build confidence
Testing triggers failures; debugging finds, analyses and removes their causes
Testing is more than test execution

nodes.title: 1.2 Why is Testing Necessary?
nodes.summary: Testing is a cost-effective way to detect defects and helps meet contractual, legal and regulatory requirements.
points: Testing is a form of quality control (QC); QA is process-oriented
A person makes an error → it produces a defect → the defect may cause a failure
Root cause: the fundamental reason a problem occurred

nodes.title: 1.3 Testing Principles
nodes.summary: Seven principles that apply across all testing.
points: Testing shows the presence, not the absence of defects
Exhaustive testing is impossible
Early testing saves time and money
Defects cluster together
Tests wear out
Testing is context dependent
Absence-of-defects fallacy

nodes.title: 1.4 Test Activities, Testware and Roles
nodes.summary: Planning, monitoring and control, analysis, design, implementation, execution and completion. Context decides how they are carried out.
points: Testware: plans, conditions, cases, scripts, data, logs, reports
Traceability links test basis, testware, results and defects
Two main roles: test management and testing

nodes.title: 1.5 Essential Skills and Good Practices
nodes.summary: Testers need domain knowledge, technical skills, communication and critical thinking.
points: Whole-team approach: quality is everyone's responsibility
Independent testers find different kinds of failures
Too much independence can isolate testers

nodes.title: 2 · Testing Throughout the SDLC
nodes.summary: How testing fits sequential, iterative and agile lifecycles; test levels and test types.
points: 6 exam questions
130 minutes

nodes.title: 2.1 Testing in the Context of an SDLC
nodes.summary: The lifecycle model affects scope, timing, documentation and automation of testing.
points: Every development activity has a matching test activity
Test-first approaches: TDD, ATDD, BDD
DevOps and CI/CD give fast feedback
Shift-left: test earlier; retrospectives improve the process

nodes.title: 2.2 Test Levels and Test Types
nodes.summary: Levels group test activities organised together; types group them by quality characteristic.
points: Levels: component, component integration, system, system integration, acceptance
Types: functional, non-functional, black-box, white-box
Confirmation testing checks a fix; regression testing checks nothing else broke

nodes.title: 2.3 Maintenance Testing
nodes.summary: Testing changes to a system in production.
points: Triggers: modification, upgrade or migration, retirement
Scope depends on risk and size of the change
Impact analysis decides regression scope

nodes.title: 3 · Static Testing
nodes.summary: Examining work products without executing them, by review or static analysis.
points: 4 exam questions
80 minutes

nodes.title: 3.1 Static Testing Basics
nodes.summary: Almost any work product can be examined statically: requirements, code, test plans, user stories.
points: Finds defects early, often before dynamic testing is possible
Finds things dynamic testing cannot, e.g. unreachable code or gaps in requirements
Static testing finds defects directly; dynamic testing finds failures

nodes.title: 3.2 Feedback and Review Process
nodes.summary: Planning, review initiation, individual review, communication and analysis, fixing and reporting.
points: Roles: manager, author, moderator, scribe, reviewer, review leader
From least to most formal: informal review, walkthrough, technical review, inspection
Success factors: clear objectives, small chunks, training, management support

nodes.title: 4 · Test Analysis and Design
nodes.summary: Techniques to derive test conditions, test cases and test data.
points: 11 exam questions, the heaviest chapter
390 minutes
Most K3 (apply) questions come from here

nodes.title: 4.1 Test Techniques Overview
nodes.summary: Techniques fall into black-box, white-box and experience-based groups.
points: Black-box: based on specified behaviour
White-box: based on internal structure
Experience-based: based on tester knowledge

nodes.title: 4.2 Black-Box Test Techniques
nodes.summary: Specification-based techniques, each with its own coverage measure.
points: Coverage = items exercised ÷ total items
You must be able to apply all four (K3)

nodes.title: Equivalence Partitioning
nodes.summary: Divide data into partitions expected to be processed the same way. One value per partition is enough.
points: Covers valid and invalid partitions
Coverage = partitions exercised ÷ total partitions
Test each invalid partition on its own

nodes.title: Boundary Value Analysis
nodes.summary: Test the edges of ordered partitions, where defects tend to hide.
points: 2-value BVA: the boundary and its nearest neighbour in the adjacent partition
3-value BVA: the boundary and both neighbours
Range 18–65 with 2-value BVA → 17, 18, 65, 66

nodes.title: Decision Table Testing
nodes.summary: Model combinations of conditions and the resulting actions. Each column is a rule.
points: n Boolean conditions → up to 2ⁿ columns
Coverage = columns exercised ÷ feasible columns
Tables can be minimised by merging columns

nodes.title: State Transition Testing
nodes.summary: Model behaviour that depends on the current state and events, e.g. lockout after failed logins.
points: All states, valid transitions (0-switch) and all transitions coverage
Valid transitions coverage is the most widely used
A state table also shows invalid transitions

nodes.title: 4.3 White-Box Test Techniques
nodes.summary: Structure-based techniques measured on code.
points: Statement coverage: executable statements exercised
Branch coverage: branches exercised
100% branch coverage implies 100% statement coverage, not the reverse

nodes.title: 4.4 Experience-Based Techniques
nodes.summary: Tester knowledge complements systematic techniques.
points: Error guessing, often as fault attacks
Exploratory testing, often session-based with a charter
Checklist-based testing

nodes.title: 4.5 Collaboration-Based Approaches
nodes.summary: Testers work with business and developers to write testable stories.
points: User stories: Card, Conversation, Confirmation
INVEST criteria
Acceptance criteria and ATDD: tests written before the code

nodes.title: 5 · Managing the Test Activities
nodes.summary: Planning, risk, monitoring, configuration and defect management.
points: 9 exam questions
335 minutes

nodes.title: 5.1 Test Planning
nodes.summary: A test plan describes objectives, resources and processes for a test project.
points: Entry criteria: preconditions to start; exit criteria: what must be achieved to finish
Estimation: ratios, extrapolation, Wideband Delphi, three-point
Test pyramid and testing quadrants guide the test mix

nodes.title: 5.2 Risk Management
nodes.summary: Risk level = likelihood × impact. Risk analysis and risk control drive risk-based testing.
points: Project risks: organisational, people, technical, supplier
Product risks: quality of the product itself, e.g. wrong calculations
Responses: mitigation, acceptance, transfer, contingency

nodes.title: 5.3 Monitoring, Control and Completion
nodes.summary: Metrics show progress against the plan so you can act on deviations.
points: Metrics: progress, defects, risk, coverage, cost
Test progress reports and test completion reports
Tailor reports to the audience

nodes.title: 5.4 Configuration Management
nodes.summary: Identify, control and track testware and test items with versions.
points: Every item uniquely identified and version controlled
Supports traceability and reproducibility

nodes.title: 5.5 Defect Management
nodes.summary: A defect report records what happened so it can be fixed.
points: Objectives: information to fix, track quality, improve the process
Content: ID, title, environment, steps, expected vs actual, severity, priority, status

nodes.title: 6 · Test Tools
nodes.summary: Tool support for testing and the benefits and risks of automation.
points: 2 exam questions
20 minutes

nodes.title: 6.1 Tool Support for Testing
nodes.summary: Tools support management, static testing, design, execution, non-functional testing, DevOps and collaboration.
points: Tools help many activities, not only execution
Choose tools to fit the context

nodes.title: 6.2 Benefits and Risks of Automation
nodes.summary: Automation saves repetitive effort but brings its own costs.
points: Benefits: less manual work, consistency, objective measures, earlier feedback
Risks: unrealistic expectations, wrong effort estimates, over-reliance, vendor issues
